mainTopic: A bride who says she was מוכת עץ, and the money at stake, then a woman who says her partner, or her baby's father, was a כהן, and what 'speaking' means.
overview: The amud opens by closing an earlier discussion: רב נחמן's view must fit with רבן גמליאל's, or two accepted rulings would clash. A new משנה follows. A bride says she lost her בתולים through an injury (מוכת עץ), and the groom says she was with a man. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her, but רבי יהושע wants proof. רבי יוחנן says they are fighting over 200 against 100, following רבי מאיר. רבי אלעזר says it is 100 against nothing, following the רבנן. The גמרא explains why each reads it that way and why two similar משניות are needed. Another משנה brings a woman seen 'speaking' with a man, and a pregnant woman, who each say the man was a כהן. זעירי says 'speaking' means she was alone with him, and רב אסי says it means relations. The גמרא defends רב אסי's reading and answers a challenge to זעירי from רב's rule about יחוד: חכמים were stricter about lineage. A new challenge from a ברייתא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two accepted rulings would clash unless the earlier answer is right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves its earlier answer. Without it, the rule 'הלכה כרב נחמן in money cases' would clash with שמואל's ruling 'הלכה כרבן גמליאל' in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it were not so, one הלכה would contradict another. We hold that the הלכה follows רב נחמן in money law. Yet in this very case רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up the answer it gave just before this. That answer showed that רב נחמן's view can live alongside רבן גמליאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that in money cases we follow רב נחמן. There is also a specific ruling from שמואל that here we follow רבן גמליאל. If the two opinions really disagreed, these two rulings would contradict each other. So they must be compatible, just as the גמרא explained.

keyTerms.meaning: One halachic ruling clashes with another
We hold / it is established for us
Monetary law (civil cases)
The final ruling follows so-and-so

phrases.english: Because if so,
one halacha would contradict another halacha.

phrases.aramaic: דְּקַיְימָא לַן הִלְכְתָא כְּרַב נַחְמָן בְּדִינֵי,
phrases.english: For we hold that the halacha follows Rav Nachman in monetary law,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and in this case Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous discussion, which tried to show that רב נחמן and רבן גמליאל agree.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier claim that רב נחמן's position fits with רבן גמליאל's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two accepted rulings: הלכה כרב נחמן בדיני, and שמואל's ruling הלכה כרבן גמליאל in this case.

steps.title: Conclusion: the earlier answer stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that its earlier way of explaining things is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that it is as we explained? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion. It confirms that רב נחמן and רבן גמליאל do not clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only way both rulings can be true is if the earlier answer is right. So the גמרא accepts that answer as final.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the point is proven
As we answered / as we explained

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'הלכה כרב נחמן בדיני' and the ruling 'הלכה כרבן גמליאל' in the bride's case can both be true. That is why the גמרא's earlier answer is accepted.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this that it is as we explained?
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's view and רבן גמליאל's view can be reconciled, as the גמרא explained.

steps.title: New משנה: 'I was injured by wood' against 'you were with a man'
steps.stepSummary: The bride says her בתולים were lost through an injury. The groom says it was through relations with a man. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her. רבי יהושע says she keeps the status of דרוסת איש until she brings proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: She says: 'I was injured by wood.' He says: 'No, you were with a man.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says: we do not live by what she says. She keeps the status of one who was with a man until she brings proof for her words.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a bride and groom who disagree about how she lost her בתולים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree she is not a בתולה. They only argue about the cause. Was it an injury (מוכת עץ) or relations with a man (דרוסת איש)? רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר accept her word. רבי יהושע puts her in the status of דרוסת איש, and she needs proof to get out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A woman whose בתולים were lost through an injury, not through relations
A woman who was with a man
She is believed
In the presumed status of
Proof

steps.confusionAlert: She is NOT claiming to be a בתולה. She admits that. She only claims her loss did not come from relations with a man.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
She says: I was injured by wood.
And he says: Not so,
rather, you were trampled by a man.
phrases.notes: "Trampled by a man" is the משנה's way of saying she had relations with a man.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by what comes from her mouth,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֲרֵי זוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת דְּרוּסַת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: rather, she is in the presumed status of one who was with a man,
until she brings proof for her words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion is closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר: the bride is believed. רבי יהושע: she is treated as דרוסת איש until she brings proof.

steps.title: What money are they fighting over?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what financial claims the bride and groom are making.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are their claims about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a question. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells us what each side says happened. It does not say how much כתובה money each side is asking for. The גמרא wants to pin that down.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion on the משנה
Their claims
About what?

phrases.english: Gemara:
What are their claims about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the money details behind the משנה's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of כתובה each side is claiming.

steps.title: Two answers: 200 against 100, or 100 against nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says she claims 200 and he says 100. רבי אלעזר says she claims 100 and he says nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is about 200 or 100. רבי אלעזר said: it is about 100 or nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Each gives a different amount at stake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, she wants a full בתולה's כתובה of 200, and he says she only gets 100. For רבי אלעזר, she wants 100, and he says she gets nothing, because she was with a man.

keyTerms.meaning: 200 זוז, the כתובה of a בתולה
A מנה, 100 זוז
And nothing at all

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: About two hundred or one hundred.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: בְּמָנֶה וְלֹא כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: About one hundred or nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: 200 against 100. רבי אלעזר: 100 against nothing.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: he follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says 200 against 100 because he follows רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר holds that a מוכת עץ gets 200 whether or not the husband knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said 200 or 100 because he holds like רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר said: whether the husband knew about her condition or did not know, she gets 200.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's answer so it can explain where it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a מוכת עץ gets a full 200. So if her claim is true, she gets 200. If the groom's claim is true, she gets the 100 of a בעולה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like...
He knew about her condition

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: About two hundred or one hundred,
because he holds like Rabbi Meir, who said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הִכִּיר בָּהּ, וּבֵין לֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ —
phrases.english: Whether he knew about her condition or did not know about her condition,
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier argument about a מוכת עץ, between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

phrases.english: she gets two hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of רבי יוחנן's answer from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן follows רבי מאיר: a מוכת עץ gets 200, so the dispute is 200 against 100.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's reason: he follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says 100 against nothing because he follows the רבנן. The רבנן hold that a מוכת עץ gets 100 whether or not the husband knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says 100 or nothing because he holds like the רבנן. They said: whether the husband knew about her condition or did not know, she gets 100.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי אלעזר's answer comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, a מוכת עץ only gets 100, so that is the most she can claim. The groom says she was with a man, which would leave her with nothing. So the dispute is 100 against nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The money amounts depend on the earlier argument about a מוכת עץ. רבי יוחנן follows רבי מאיר, which gives 200 against 100. רבי אלעזר follows the רבנן, which gives 100 against nothing.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בְּמָנֶה וְלֹא כְּלוּם —
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says: About one hundred or nothing at all,
because he holds like the Rabbis, who say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הִכִּיר בָּהּ, בֵּין לֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ —
phrases.english: Whether he knew about her condition or did not know about her condition,
she gets one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches step 6, now explaining רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר follows the רבנן: a מוכת עץ gets 100, so the dispute is 100 against nothing.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יוחנן explain the משנה like רבי אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why רבי אלעזר did not follow רבי יוחנן's reading, since רבי אלעזר wants the משנה to match the רבנן. It now asks why רבי יוחנן did not follow רבי אלעזר's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי אלעזר did not say what רבי יוחנן said, because he wants to explain the משנה like the רבנן. But what is the reason that רבי יוחנן did not say what רבי אלעזר said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. One side of their disagreement makes sense, so it asks for the reason behind the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Explaining a משנה like the רבנן is the more natural choice, so רבי אלעזר's reading needs no defense. רבי יוחנן chose to explain the משנה like רבי מאיר, a single opinion. The גמרא wants to know what pushed him to do that.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense. Introduces the side that is easy to understand before asking about the other side.
Establishes it, meaning he explains the משנה as following a certain opinion.
The Sages, here the majority who argue with רבי מאיר.
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Elazar
did not say like Rabbi Yochanan
because he establishes it according to the Rabbis.
But Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason
that he did not say like Rabbi Elazar?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לֹא קָאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two readings given in steps 6–7 and asks why רבי יוחנן chose his.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן did not adopt רבי אלעזר's reading, which follows the רבנן.

steps.title: Under רבי אלעזר's reading, both claims would be the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that a woman married as a בתולה who turns out to be a בעולה still gets a מנה. So in רבי אלעזר's reading he would say a מנה and she would say a מנה, and there would be nothing to argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if a man married a woman thinking she was a בתולה and she turned out to be a בעולה, she still gets a כתובה of a מנה. Here, then, he says a מנה and she says a מנה. What difference is there between his claim and her claim?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that רבי אלעזר's reading would not work for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says the husband claims she gets nothing. But רבי יוחנן holds that even a בעולה gets a מנה. Under the רבנן, the injured bride also gets only a מנה, so both sides would claim the same amount and the משנה would have no argument. That forced רבי יוחנן to read the משנה like רבי מאיר, where the claims are 200 against 100.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he is of the opinion.
With the assumed status of a virgin.
A woman who has already had relations, a non-virgin.
A מנה, 100 זוז, the smaller כתובה amount.
A claim.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן is now arguing with the רבנן about the מוכת עץ. His point is only that if the husband can't claim 'nothing,' then under the רבנן both sides would say a מנה.

phrases.english: He holds: if he married her as a presumed virgin
and she was found to be a non-virgin,
she has a marriage contract of a maneh.
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 זוז, half of the regular 200.

phrases.english: Here, he says a maneh,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, if you read it the way רבי אלעזר does.

phrases.english: and she says a maneh,
what difference is there between his claim
and her claim?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כְּנָסָהּ בְּחֶזְקַת בְּתוּלָה וְנִמְצֵאת בְּעוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8's question about רבי יוחנן's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן holds a בעולה still gets a מנה, so under the רבנן both sides would claim a מנה and there would be no argument. He therefore reads the משנה like רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why would רבי יוחנן need two similar disputes?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר can explain why the תנא teaches two similar disputes: each one rejects a different later view, one of רמי בר חמא and one of רב ששת. But רבי יוחנן agrees with רב ששת, so why does he need both disputes?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי אלעזר. That is why the משנה teaches two cases. One rejects the view of רמי בר חמא, and the other rejects what רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב ששת. But according to רבי יוחנן, why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's reading. It argues that only רבי אלעזר's reading explains why the תנא teaches two similar disputes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is about an injured bride, and the one before it is about a bride who says she was raped after betrothal. For רבי אלעזר, each has a job. Ours shows an injured bride still claims a מנה, against רמי בר חמא. The earlier one shows the husband can claim she gets nothing, against רב ששת. רבי יוחנן agrees with רב ששת, as step 9 showed, so the earlier משנה seems to lose its purpose for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, here two similar disputes.
To exclude, meaning to reject a certain opinion.
Why do I need it? Asks why something is written when it seems unnecessary.
That is why it teaches.

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא often tests a reading of a משנה by asking whether it explains why the משנה teaches every case. A reading that leaves one case with no purpose is under pressure.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Elazar,
that is why it teaches two:
phrases.notes: The two are our משנה and the one just before it, where the bride says she was raped after betrothal.

phrases.english: one to exclude the view of Rami bar Chama,
phrases.notes: רמי בר חמא held that if the husband didn't know about the injury, she gets nothing.

phrases.english: and one to exclude

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת.
phrases.english: that which Rav Chiya bar Avin said Rav Sheshet said.
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 9: a woman found to be a בעולה still gets a מנה.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
why do I need two?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר — הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוחנן's reading, the גמרא attacks it from a new angle: why the משנה repeats a similar dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of the משנה (200 against 100).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's reading gives each of the two disputes a purpose: one rejects רמי בר חמא and one rejects רב ששת. רבי יוחנן agrees with רב ששת, so one of the two disputes seems to have no purpose for him.

steps.title: Each dispute shows the strength of a different side
steps.stepSummary: Both disputes are needed. The first shows that רבי יהושע doesn't believe her even when she has a מיגו. The second shows that רבן גמליאל believes her even when she has no מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: One dispute shows how far רבן גמליאל goes, and one shows how far רבי יהושע goes. The first dispute shows רבי יהושע's strength: even though she has a מיגו, she is not believed. The second dispute shows רבן גמליאל's strength: even though she has no מיגו, she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10: why would רבי יוחנן need the תנא to teach two similar disputes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case she has a מיגו, an extra reason to believe her, and רבי יהושע still says she is not believed. That shows how strict he is. In the second case she has no מיגו, and רבן גמליאל still believes her. That shows how far he trusts her.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you his strength, meaning how far a Tanna is willing to take his view
'Since.' Since she could have made another claim that would win just as much, we lean toward believing the claim she made
She is believed
The first one / the last one

steps.whatToRemember: The two disputes are not repeats. One shows that רבי יהושע doesn't believe her even with a מיגו. The other shows that רבן גמליאל believes her even without one.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip the two. The case WITH a מיגו shows רבי יהושע's strength, because he still doesn't believe her. The case WITHOUT a מיגו shows רבן גמליאל's strength, because he still does believe her.

phrases.english: One is to show you the strength of Rabban Gamliel,
and one is to show you the strength of Rabbi Yehoshua.
The first one shows you the strength of Rabbi Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: The first dispute is where she says she was forced after the betrothal. The second is where she says she was injured by wood.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מִיגּוֹ —
phrases.english: that even though one could argue a miggo,
she is not believed.
The last one shows you the strength of Rabban Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא לְמֵימַר מִיגּוֹ,
phrases.english: that even though one cannot argue a miggo,
she is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each repetition teaches a different point (לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוחנן agrees with רב ששת, the earlier dispute (the previous משנה, where she says she was forced after the betrothal) looked unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both disputes are needed: one shows how strict רבי יהושע is even with a מיגו, and the other shows how lenient רבן גמליאל is even without one.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman seen speaking with an unknown man
steps.stepSummary: A woman was seen with an unknown man and says he was a כהן. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says she is treated as if she was with a נתין or a ממזר until she brings proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If people saw a woman speaking with a man and asked her who he was, and she said he was so-and-so and a כהן, רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says we don't go by what she says. She is treated as one who was with a נתין or a ממזר until she proves her words.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is another dispute about whether a woman is believed about herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What is at stake is her status. If the man was a כהן, she stays fit to marry a כהן. If he was a נתין or a ממזר, she becomes unfit. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר trust her word, but רבי יהושע wants real proof.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his nature, meaning who is he and what is his lineage?
A descendant of the Gibeonites. Relations with him make a woman unfit to marry a כהן
A child of a forbidden relationship. Relations with him also make a woman unfit to marry a כהן
In the presumed status of
We don't live by her mouth, meaning we don't rely on her word alone

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If they saw her speaking with someone,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל אִישׁ זֶה?
phrases.english: and they said to her: What is the nature of this man?
[She answered:] He is so-and-so, and he is a priest.
phrases.notes: The words 'she answered' are not written, but the משנה assumes them.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by her mouth,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֲרֵי זוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת בְּעוּלָה לְנָתִין וּלְמַמְזֵר,
phrases.english: rather, she is presumed to have been with a Gibeonite or a mamzer,
until she brings proof for her words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a related dispute about believing a woman
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר: she is believed that the man was a כהן. רבי יהושע: she is presumed to have been with a נתין or a ממזר until she brings proof.

steps.title: Second case: a pregnant woman names the father
steps.stepSummary: A pregnant woman says the baby is from a כהן. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says she is presumed pregnant from a נתין or a ממזר until she brings proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was pregnant and people asked her whose baby it is, and she said it was from so-and-so, a כהן, רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says we don't go by her word. She is presumed pregnant from a נתין or a ממזר until she proves her words.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case with the same dispute. This time the woman is pregnant, and the question is who the father is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we know for sure that she had relations, because she is pregnant. The only question is with whom. The same disagreement applies to her status, and the second case also raises the question of the baby's status.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman
Fetus, an unborn baby
Proof

phrases.english: If she was pregnant,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל עוּבָּר זֶה?
phrases.english: and they said to her: What is the nature of this fetus?
[She said:] From so-and-so, and he is a priest.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by her mouth,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֲרֵי זוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת לְנָתִין וּלְמַמְזֵר,
phrases.english: rather, she is presumed pregnant from a Gibeonite or a mamzer,
until she brings proof for her words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same dispute: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her that the father is a כהן. רבי יהושע presumes the father was a נתין or a ממזר until she brings proof.

steps.title: What does 'speaking' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'speaking' with a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What does 'speaking' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about one word in the משנה. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says she was 'speaking' with a man. That can't be the whole story, because just talking wouldn't make anyone worry about her status. So the גמרא wants to know what actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?
Speaking

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is 'speaking'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the משנה in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word מדברת in the משנה means

steps.title: Two answers: secluded or had relations
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says it means she was alone with him. רב אסי says it means she had relations with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: she was secluded with him. רב אסי said: she had relations with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain the word 'speaking' in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For זעירי, we only know she was alone with the man, and it's not certain anything happened. For רב אסי, we know relations happened. So according to זעירי, the dispute is even about a case where it's not clear anything happened at all.

keyTerms.meaning: She was secluded, alone with a man
She had relations

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said: She was secluded [with him],
Rav Asi said: She had relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זעירי: 'speaking' means she was secluded with him. רב אסי: it means she had relations.

steps.title: Why say 'speaking' if רב אסי means relations?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'speaking' fits זעירי well, but why would the משנה use it if it means relations, as רב אסי says?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to זעירי, which is why the משנה says 'speaking.' But according to רב אסי, why say 'speaking'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's reading because it doesn't match the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was only alone with him, 'speaking' is a fair way to put it, because maybe they only talked. But if relations happened, the word 'speaking' seems wrong. So the challenge is against רב אסי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense according to... (this opens a contrast)
That is why it teaches...

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Ze'eiri,
that is why it teaches 'speaking.'
But according to Rav Asi, what is 'speaking'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's answer from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's explanation that מדברת means נבעלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'speaking' fits seclusion, but it doesn't seem to fit relations.

steps.title: A polite way of speaking, backed by a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The משנה used a clean, polite expression, just as a פסוק describes relations using the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a clean way of speaking, as it is written: 'She eats and wipes her mouth and says: I have done no wrong.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. 'Speaking' is a polite way to describe relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה avoided saying it directly and chose a refined word. A פסוק does the same thing: it describes relations as eating and wiping the mouth. So רב אסי's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A refined, clean way of saying something
As it is written
Wrongdoing, sin

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי reads 'speaking' as seclusion. רב אסי reads it as relations, and the משנה just chose a polite word, the way the פסוק in משלי does.

phrases.english: It is refined language,
as it is written:
"She eats and wipes her mouth
and says: I have done no wrong."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as a polite expression (לישנא מעליא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Speaking' seemed to fit only seclusion, as זעירי says.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to רב אסי, the משנה said 'speaking' as a polite word for relations, like the פסוק in משלי.

steps.title: Why would the משנה need two cases according to רב אסי?
steps.stepSummary: According to זעירי, the two cases in the משנה teach different things. According to רב אסי, both cases seem to involve relations, so one looks extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to זעירי that the משנה teaches two cases, 'speaking' and 'pregnant.' But according to רב אסי, why do we need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי. If 'speaking' already means relations, the pregnant case seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For זעירי, the cases are different: 'speaking' is only being alone together, and 'pregnant' is clear proof of relations. For רב אסי, both cases involve relations, so the משנה seems to repeat itself. The גמרא asks what the second case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this works for one view, but not the other' challenge)
Why do I need two (cases)?
A pregnant woman

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Ze'eiri,
that this is why it teaches two cases:
'speaking' and 'pregnant.'
phrases.notes: These are the two cases in the משנה: the woman seen 'speaking' with a man, and the unmarried woman who is pregnant.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Asi,
why do I need two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 17 explained why the משנה would use the word 'speaking' for relations. Now the גמרא asks a second question against רב אסי: the משנה seems to repeat itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's explanation that 'speaking' means relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both 'speaking' and 'pregnant' mean she had relations, the second case is extra and seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One case is about the woman, the other is about her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The 'speaking' case teaches that the woman herself is fit for a כהן. The 'pregnant' case teaches that her daughter is fit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One case teaches that she herself is fit, and the other teaches that her daughter is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. Each case teaches a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve relations, but they answer different questions. 'Speaking' teaches that the woman is believed, so she may marry a כהן. 'Pregnant' teaches that the child born from that pregnancy is also fit.

keyTerms.meaning: To declare fit (here: fit to marry a כהן)
Her daughter

steps.confusionAlert: 'Her' and 'her daughter' are two separate questions. A woman may be believed about herself, and there can still be a separate question about the child.

phrases.english: One, to declare her fit.
And one, to declare her daughter fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא, לְהַכְשִׁיר בָּהּ. וַחֲדָא, לְהַכְשִׁיר בְּבִתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each case teaches a separate law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases seemed to teach the same thing: that she had relations and is believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Speaking' is about the woman being fit. 'Pregnant' is about her daughter being fit.

steps.title: What about the view that the daughter is unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works only if whoever says the mother is fit also says the daughter is fit. Some say the mother is fit but the daughter is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says that, according to whoever declares her fit, he also declares her daughter fit. But according to the one who says that, even according to whoever declares her fit, he declares her daughter unfit, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 19. It points to an opinion that would break that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known dispute about how far רבן גמליאל's ruling reaches. One view says it covers the daughter too. The other says only the mother is fit, but not the daughter. According to the second view, the pregnant case could not be teaching that the daughter is fit, so the extra case is again unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view)
Declares unfit
What is there to say? (the answer seems to fail)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says:
according to the one who declares her fit,
phrases.notes: This means רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר, who believe the woman in the משנה.

phrases.english: he also declares her daughter fit.
But according to the one who says:
according to the one who declares her fit,
he declares her daughter unfit,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the pregnant case teaches that the daughter is fit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that the daughter stays unfit even when the mother is believed, the pregnant case cannot teach that the daughter is fit. So the second case is again unexplained.

steps.title: רב אסי holds that the daughter is fit too
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי follows the view that whoever declares the mother fit also declares the daughter fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי holds like the one who said that, according to whoever declares her fit, he also declares her daughter fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: רב אסי holds the opinion that keeps step 19's answer working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only matters for someone who holds the other view. Since רב אסי holds that the daughter is fit too, the pregnant case really does teach something new for him. Both cases are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds like the one who said

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אסי, the משנה needs both cases. 'Speaking' (relations) makes the woman fit for a כהן, and 'pregnant' makes her daughter fit. This works because רב אסי holds that the daughter's status follows the mother's.

phrases.english: Rav Asi holds like the one who said:
according to the one who declares her fit,
he also declares her daughter fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places רב אסי on one side of a known dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי might hold that the daughter is unfit, which would make the pregnant case extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אסי holds that the daughter is fit too, so both cases are needed.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges זעירי from רב's rule about seclusion
steps.stepSummary: רב ruled that being alone together does not make a woman forbidden. So how can רבי יהושע, according to זעירי, treat a woman who was only secluded as having had relations with a פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: According to זעירי, who said 'speaking' means she was secluded, and רבי יהושע said she is not believed: but didn't רב say that we give lashes for seclusion but we do not forbid a woman because of seclusion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks זעירי's explanation. רב פפא brings a ruling of רב that seems to contradict how זעירי reads רבי יהושע. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to זעירי, the woman in the משנה was only alone with the man, yet רבי יהושע treats her as having had relations with a פסול. But רב said seclusion is punished with lashes and does not make a woman forbidden. Seclusion alone is not treated as proof of relations. So why does רבי יהושע treat it as proof?

keyTerms.meaning: She secluded herself (was alone with a man)
She is not believed
We give lashes
Forbidden seclusion of a man and woman alone together
We make her forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
According to Ze'eiri, who said:
What is 'speaking'? She secluded herself,
and Rabbi Yehoshua said she is not believed,
but didn't Rav say:
We give lashes for seclusion,
but we do not make her forbidden because of seclusion!
phrases.notes: He means a married woman who was alone with another man is not forbidden to her husband because of that alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב אסי, the גמרא turns to challenge זעירי's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's reading that 'speaking' means seclusion, together with רבי יהושע's ruling that she is not believed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ruled that seclusion alone does not make a woman forbidden, so seclusion is not treated as proof of relations. Yet according to זעירי, רבי יהושע treats a secluded woman as having had relations with a פסול.

steps.title: Does רב disagree with רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב's ruling, that seclusion alone does not forbid a woman, goes against רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב does not follow רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the problem from step 22 and states it outright. Maybe רב's ruling simply disagrees with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a woman is not made forbidden just because she was alone with a man. According to זעירי, רבי יהושע treats a woman who was only secluded as if she had relations with a פסול. So the גמרא proposes that רב and רבי יהושע disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? This word opens a suggested conclusion that the גמרא will usually push back on.
Being alone together in a private place. This is the topic of רב's ruling.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is not like רבי יהושע?
phrases.notes: "It" means רב's ruling from step 22, that being alone together does not make a woman forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the proposed result of the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב's ruling fits with רבי יהושע as זעירי explains him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seclusion either makes a woman forbidden or it does not. רב says it does not, while רבי יהושע (per זעירי) treats it as a problem, so they seem to disagree.

steps.title: Lineage has a stricter standard
steps.stepSummary: רב can agree with רבי יהושע, because חכמים were stricter about lineage than about forbidding a wife to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say רב follows רבי יהושע. חכמים set a higher standard for matters of lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no real disagreement. The two rulings are about different kinds of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling is about whether a wife becomes forbidden to her husband because of seclusion, and there she does not. רבי יהושע's ruling is about whether a woman may marry a כהן, which is a question of lineage, and there חכמים were extra strict. So the same seclusion can be harmless for the marriage but still disqualify her from כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say. This phrase rejects the suggestion and shows the two views can fit together.
A higher or stricter standard that חכמים added.
Lineage, meaning family purity, for example who is fit to marry a כהן.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same set of facts can have different outcomes in different areas of הלכה. Lineage is guarded more strictly.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהושע says the woman is forbidden to her husband. The stricter rule is only about lineage, meaning her fitness to marry a כהן.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows רבי יהושע,
they made a higher standard for lineage.
phrases.notes: "They" means חכמים. Being alone with a man does not forbid her to her husband, but it can still make her unfit for a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 23 that רב disagrees with רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between areas of law: forbidding a wife to her husband versus lineage for כהונה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seclusion should have the same result everywhere, so רב and רבי יהושע must disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים were stricter about יוחסין. Seclusion does not forbid a wife to her husband, but it can disqualify a woman from marrying a כהן.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a woman seen entering seclusion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge from a ברייתא about a woman seen going into a private place with a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If people saw that she entered with one man into a private place...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the rest of the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי tells us a source is about to argue against what was just said. The case is a woman who was only seen entering seclusion, which is the same kind of case זעירי's reading of רבי יהושע deals with. How it challenges the discussion becomes clear once the rest of the ברייתא is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged. This word introduces a ברייתא brought as an objection.
A hidden or private place.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If they saw that she entered with one man into a private place,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רָאוּהָ שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה עִם אֶחָד לְסֵתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 24, the גמרא begins a new objection from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The current understanding of seclusion cases. The exact target becomes clear when the ברייתא continues.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא deals with a woman seen only entering seclusion, and its ruling will be compared with the discussion so far.
